name: ZipfLaw.zipf_summable_iff
theorem_title: The Zipf p-series converges exactly for $s>1$
formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipf_summable_iff (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) :
    Summable (fun k : ℕ => 1 / ((k : ℝ) + 1) ^ s) ↔ 1 < s := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
natural_language_statement: For a real exponent $s\ge0$, the series $\sum_{k=1}^{\infty} k^{-s}$ is summable if and only if $s>1$. This is the convergence criterion in the infinite-extension theorem, isolated for reuse in both its convergent and divergent branches.
source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.

name: ZipfLaw.zipf_genHarmonic_tendsto_zeta
theorem_title: For $s>1$, the Zipf harmonic sums tend to $\zeta(s)$
formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipf_genHarmonic_tendsto_zeta (s : ℝ) (hs : 1 < s) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => ((genHarmonic N s : ℝ) : ℂ)) Filter.atTop
      (nhds (riemannZeta s)) := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
natural_language_statement: If $s>1$, the generalized harmonic partial sums $H_{N,s}=\sum_{k=1}^{N}k^{-s}$ converge to Riemann's zeta function $\zeta(s)$. The formal limit takes place in $\mathbb C$ after casting the real sums, because Mathlib's `riemannZeta` is complex-valued.
source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.

name: ZipfLaw.zipf_genHarmonic_tendsto_atTop
theorem_title: For $0\le s\le1$, the Zipf harmonic sums tend to infinity
formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipf_genHarmonic_tendsto_atTop (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hs1 : s ≤ 1) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => genHarmonic N s) Filter.atTop Filter.atTop := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
natural_language_statement: For every real exponent $0\le s\le1$, the generalized harmonic sums $H_{N,s}$ tend to $+\infty$ as $N\to\infty$. In particular no finite normalizing constant can extend these finite Zipf laws to infinitely many ranks.
source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.

name: ZipfLaw.genHarmonic_pos
theorem_title: A nonempty generalized harmonic sum is positive
formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem genHarmonic_pos (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) (s : ℝ) : 0 < genHarmonic N s := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
natural_language_statement: For every integer $N\ge1$ and real exponent $s$, the generalized harmonic sum $H_{N,s}=\sum_{k=1}^{N} k^{-s}$ is strictly positive. This ensures that the common normalizing factor can be cancelled and logarithms of supported Zipf probabilities are well-defined.
source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.

name: ZipfLaw.zipfPMF_moment
theorem_title: All finite Zipf moments are ratios of shifted harmonic sums
formal_statement:
namespace ZipfLaw

theorem zipfPMF_moment (N : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (p : ℕ) :
    (∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 N, (k : ℝ) ^ p * zipfPMF N s k) =
      genHarmonic N (s - p) / genHarmonic N s := by sorry

end ZipfLaw
natural_language_statement: For every cutoff $N\in\mathbb N$, real exponent $s$, and integer moment order $p\ge0$, the finite Zipf law satisfies $\sum_{k=1}^{N} k^p f(k;s,N)=H_{N,s-p}/H_{N,s}$. The identity includes $N=0$ under Lean's convention for division by zero. The first and second moment formulas in the mission are its special cases.
source: Wikipedia, "Zipf's law", https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zipf%27s_law, section "Formal definition"; auxiliary lemma for the original ZipfLaw mission, derived from its displayed PMF and generalized harmonic sum.
